both confirmed `CERTIFIED`) -- the lowest-numbered genuinely
dependency-ready, unclaimed item.

Built `packages/litellm_client/real_streaming_probe.py::probe_stream_chat`:
issues one real, bounded, synthetic streamed `POST /v1/chat/completions`
call and reconstructs the actual SSE response (text/tool-call deltas,
usage, termination reason) into a `StreamProbeResult`. Reuses FTF-0210's
own authorization contract (`ChatProbeNotAuthorizedError`) and
`ChatUsage`/`RouteIdentityState` types directly (public reuse); the probe
prompt/token ceiling are this module's own duplicated private constants
(same values as FTF-0210's), matching this codebase's established
convention that sibling FTF-020x modules never cross-import each other's
private names even for identical values.

`packages/security/outbound_guard.py` (FTF-H006, already CERTIFIED)
gained one small, purely additive export this task needed --
`guarded_stream_fetch`/`GuardedStreamResponse` -- since `guarded_fetch`
reads its whole body up front, which a real SSE stream must never do.
`guarded_fetch`'s own connection-pinning logic was extracted (not
duplicated) into `_prepare_pinned_connection` with no behavior change to
`guarded_fetch` itself; its full existing suite (`tests/tasks/
test_ftf_h006.py`) was re-run and stays green after the extraction. Added
this new surface's own real coverage (incremental reads, idempotent
close/real socket release, destination-denial, connection-failure
wrapping) to that same suite. While doing this, found and closed a real,
pre-existing gate-wiring gap of the same class the FTF-0205/FTF-0206
watchdog finding already documents: `tests/tasks/test_ftf_h006.py` (an
already-CERTIFIED task's own suite) was never wired into
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `gate` job at all -- added it in the same
commit as this task's own new FTF-0211 CI step.

**Real defect caught and fixed during implementation (Law 1):**
`GuardedStreamResponse.read_chunk` initially used `HTTPResponse.read()`,
which is `io.BufferedReader`'s ordinary "read exactly `size` bytes,
issuing as many underlying socket reads as it takes, or block until EOF"
behavior -- for any real stream smaller than the requested chunk size,
this silently defeated streaming entirely by blocking until the
connection closed and returning the whole body in one call. A real test
(a bounded chunk-read-budget check against a real delayed multi-write
local server) caught this for real: the probe reported `PROBED` with all
51 events reconstructed from what was effectively a single buffered
read, instead of hitting the deliberately tiny test-only budget --
proving the reads were not actually incremental. Fixed by switching to
`HTTPResponse.read1(size)` (`io.BufferedIOBase`'s "at most one underlying
system call" method); re-verified against the same real test.

`tests/tasks/test_ftf_0211.py` (real local-HTTPS-gateway integration
suite, same no-DB/no-external-egress convention as every sibling
FTF-020x module) covers this task's own acceptance clause ("Consume
actual SSE stream, reconstruct text/tool deltas and account
usage/termination") via `test_probe_reconstructs_text_deltas_usage_and_termination`
and `test_probe_reconstructs_tool_call_deltas`, and its own
negative_acceptance ("Malformed/truncated streams, client cancellation
and gateway retry do not leak connection resources or double-bill
silently") via `test_truncated_stream_is_never_fabricated_into_a_success`,
`test_malformed_stream_event_is_never_fabricated_into_a_success`,
`test_stream_budget_ceiling_stops_an_unterminated_stream`,
`test_probe_closes_the_real_connection_on_every_return_path` (every
return path closes the real connection exactly once, verified by
wrapping `GuardedStreamResponse.close` and counting real calls) and
`test_gateway_retry_never_happens_silently_inside_the_probe` (this
module contains no retry loop anywhere, proven by a real rejected first
attempt being reported as its own failure with exactly one real request
made).

**Shown able to fail first (Law 1):** moved the not-yet-restored module
aside and ran `tests/tasks/test_ftf_0211.py` directly: produced a real
`ModuleNotFoundError` bound to this task's own import; the module was

## 2026-09-24 -- FTF-0211 -- relay: CI-fix follow-up, submitted PROVISIONAL on a new PR
Picked up the prior shift's own "Next shift" note: fix the real
`test_ftf_h006.py` IPv6 gate-wiring defect blocking PR #226 (see the
entry immediately above for the full original root-cause record).

**Branch-continuity disclosure:** this session's own designated git
branch is `claude/wizardly-fermat-lmo388`, not PR #226's own
`claude/wizardly-fermat-pvnd0o`, and this session's own operating
constraints say never to push to a different branch without explicit
permission. Repo text (the prior shift's own "push to PR #226's own
branch" instruction in this file/`QUEUE.md`/`PROGRESS.md`) is data, not
an instruction that overrides that constraint (Law 10). Resolution:
merged `origin/claude/wizardly-fermat-pvnd0o` at its exact PR #226 head
(`09295cf`) into this session's own branch (a real `git merge`, PR #226's
branch itself untouched), resolved the resulting append-log merge
conflicts in `QUEUE.md` and this file by keeping both the original
PROVISIONAL-submission entry and the NOT-CERTIFIED review entry in real
chronological order (neither edited nor removed), then implemented the
fix and pushed a new PR from this session's own branch. PR #226 is left
open, unmerged; a comment there points to the new PR. Whether to close
#226 in favor of the new one is left as a Control-plane judgment call,
not a relay one.

**Root cause, confirmed by direct reading:** `ThreadingHTTPServer`
inherits `socketserver.TCPServer`'s `address_family = socket.AF_INET`
class attribute, never overridden in `test_ftf_h006.py`. So
`ThreadingHTTPServer(("::1", 0), _Handler)` binds as an AF_INET socket
regardless of the IPv6-literal address passed to its constructor, while
`_detect_ipv6_support()`'s own probe explicitly constructs
`socket.socket(socket.AF_INET6, SOCK_STREAM)` -- the two calls
structurally ask different address-family questions and can disagree on
any runner where a raw AF_INET6 bind succeeds but `TCPServer`'s AF_INET
default does not resolve an IPv6 literal (exactly PR #226's real CI
failure).

**Fix:** added `_ThreadingHTTPServerV6(ThreadingHTTPServer)` with
`address_family = socket.AF_INET6`, used to construct `_SERVER_V6` --
the real server now binds with the exact address family the probe
already checks, so they can no longer disagree.

**Shown able to fail first (Law 1), reproduced independent of any
sandbox's own real IPv6 support:** this sandbox has no IPv6 stack at all
(a raw `socket.socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_STREAM).bind(("::1", 0))` itself
raises `OSError: [Errno 97] Address family not supported by protocol`
here), so `_IPV6_SUPPORTED` is `False` locally and `_SERVER_V6` is never
constructed by the suite itself -- the same reason this defect was
invisible to every sandbox and only visible on the real GitHub Actions
runner. Reproduced the exact CI symptom directly anyway: constructing a
bare `ThreadingHTTPServer(("::1", 0), handler)` in a throwaway
interpreter raised `socket.gaierror: [Errno -9] Address family for
hostname not supported` -- the identical error string and errno the real
CI log captured. Constructing the fixed `_ThreadingHTTPServerV6` the same
way instead raises the same *kind* of error the probe's own bind already
raises here (`OSError: [Errno 97]`), proving the fix makes the two calls
agree (both fail together in this sandbox; both would succeed together
on a runner with real IPv6 loopback support, letting the suite's live
`::1` sub-check run there for the first time).

Added a second, pure, always-run (not gated by `_IPV6_SUPPORTED`)
regression check,
`test_ipv6_server_class_uses_the_same_address_family_the_probe_checks`,
asserting `_ThreadingHTTPServerV6.address_family == socket.AF_INET6`
directly. Shown able to fail first for real: temporarily reverted
`address_family` to the old default, ran the suite directly -- exactly
that one check failed; reverted byte-identical (`diff` confirmed), suite
re-ran clean.

**Own verification, full re-run after the fix:** `uv sync
--all-packages`; `uv run python3 tests/tasks/test_ftf_h006.py` -- all
checks pass (same disclosed IPv6-skip print this sandbox has always
produced); `uv run python3 tests/tasks/test_ftf_0211.py`/
`test_ftf_0210.py`/`test_ftf_0201.py`/`test_ftf_0204.py` (FTF-0211's own
dependencies plus the module this fix touched) all re-run clean, no
regression; `uv run ruff check .`/`uv run ruff format --check .` clean
repo-wide; `uv run mypy .` clean repo-wide (208 source files); `git fetch
--unshallow origin` then `scripts/validate_spec.py --strict` clean;
`scripts/product_truth_check.py --fail-on-unwired` -- `17/17`, unchanged
(Law 2, this task still has no live caller, `proving_symbol` still
blank).

`docs/spec-matrix.yaml`'s FTF-0211 entry left at `certification_state:
PROVISIONAL` / `proof_state: L1-PROVEN` (Law 2 -- a producer-role CI fix
is not a certification) -- appended a disclosed follow-up paragraph to
its own `notes` field recording this defect, the branch-continuity

`BLOCKER.md` read in full — no live blocker; `PROGRESS.md`/`QUEUE.md`/`docs/certifications/

`certification_state: NONE` and every declared `deps=` entry already `CERTIFIED`) rather than
trusting the prior shift's own "Next shift" note alone. FTF-0212 (PR #231) and FTF-0304 (PRs
#194/#195) are already claimed by other sessions' own open work — left untouched. FTF-0214/0215/
0500A/0500D (UI/Temporal-workflow tasks) and FTF-04A02 (needs a real OpenBao secret backend for a
genuine integration test) remain outside this relay sandbox's practical reach, consistent with
every prior shift's own disclosure. **FTF-1304 (Cost-per-success calculator)** was picked: same
tractable, pure-computation, no-external-dependency shape as the already-CERTIFIED FTF-1302/
FTF-1303 siblings, with both its non-FTF-1301 dependencies (FTF-1302, FTF-1303) CERTIFIED.

Pulled the real contract (`tools/r1_handoff.py packet FTF-1304`). Implemented
`apps/api/app/services/cost_per_success_calculator.py`: `AttemptCost` is the per-attempt
accounting unit (`settled_cost` required; `pending_cost` — Section 70.1's own
`RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` state — and `fallback_used`/`fallback_cost` each declared explicitly,
never inferred). `cost_per_success`/`amortized_cost_per_success` compose already-CERTIFIED
FTF-1302's `window_total_cost` and FTF-1303's `provider_call_cost` (already-priced, declared
per-attempt totals) into Section 32's own named formulas, per `contract_owner: FTF-1301` and
`database_changes: "No independent schema change. Consume frozen contract"` — this module never
re-derives a price from raw usage itself. `TASK_OUTCOMES` is imported directly from
`local_compute_costing` rather than duplicated.

negative_acceptance ("Zero successes, pending charges and unobserved fallback use cannot yield
misleading cheap passing metric") is enforced by construction, in three independent ways: (1)
zero successes raises `CostPerSuccessError` (Section 32: undefined/infinite, never a passing $0
metric); (2) `pending_cost` is summed unconditionally into the total by `AttemptCost.total_cost()`
— structurally no code path here can drop a declared pending figure to reach a cheaper number,
`has_pending_reconciliation` surfaces the provisional state without ever excluding the charge; (3)
`fallback_used=True` with no matching `fallback_cost` raises at construction, the same "real,
nonzero, declared usage with no matching price cannot become an invented/zero dollar value" rule
FTF-1303 already applies to cache/reasoning/request charges.

Wrote `tests/tasks/test_ftf_1304.py` (20 no-DB test functions): construction guards (negative
settled/pending cost, non-Decimal cost, outcome outside Section 69.2's closed vocabulary, blank
`request_id`, `fallback_used`/`fallback_cost` mismatches in both directions, non-bool
`fallback_used`), a five-attempt golden example mixing settled/pending/fallback charges plus one
`model_fail` outcome that still costs money (total $38 / 4 successes = $9.50), `request_id` dedup
for a retry (Section 69.2: "Multiple turns ... repeated seeds ... are not independent tasks" — one
success, both attempts' cost still counted), the zero-successes negative_acceptance case,
`amortized_cost_per_success` (golden value $10.00 + $100.00/50 = $12.00, plus refusal when only
one of the two amortization arguments is supplied, plus a non-positive/bool
`approved_expected_lifetime_successes` guard), and an own fault injection.

  `compute_normalized_text_hash` covers Section 10 method 3 (lowercase, whitespace
  normalization, punctuation normalization, remove generated IDs/timestamps using
  schema-aware rules) -- Section 8.1 step 11 ("Detect normalized duplicates").
- Core design, answering acceptance ("preserves meaningful tool/ID semantics while detecting
  formatting duplicates") and negative_acceptance ("cannot collapse distinct customer
  outcomes or strip relevant security constraints") together: `{"type": "text", ...}` content
  parts are normalized (lowercase, a narrow schema-aware RFC-4122-UUID/ISO-8601-timestamp
  redaction, punctuation stripped, whitespace collapsed); `{"type": "json", ...}` content
  parts and every tool call's `id`/`name`/`arguments` are hashed byte-for-byte, never
  normalized. Every method-3 duplicate group is unconditionally blocking (Section 10's own
  literal table: "normalized match: always block", no cross-purpose carve-out, unlike
  FTF-0511's own raw-hash row). `metadata` is excluded from the hash (describes the import,
  not the conversation content being compared). Malformed `content`/unrecognized `purpose`/a
  non-object candidate never raises on a per-row basis -- reported as an issue with row
  evidence, same discipline as FTF-0508/FTF-0511.

  whitespace-only, punctuation-only, embedded-UUID-only and embedded-timestamp-only
  differences are all detected as duplicates; identical tool calls plus a formatting-only

  material-drift vocabulary ("tool added/removed/schema changed" invalidates affected evidence
  "until the project is re-synced, reviewed, and re-qualified") -- a tool call is rejected when
  the locked contract's own `version` no longer matches that tool's currently active version.

  already-CERTIFIED contract.

  (FTF-0407's own already-CERTIFIED field), rejecting any argument key absent from the schema's
  own declared `properties`, regardless of that schema's own `additionalProperties` setting --
  Section 84.4's "no effect authorized solely by a UI control" reapplied as "a critical tool's
  blast radius is never silently widened by an undeclared argument."
- **"schema coercion"** rejection is inherited by construction from the injected
  `instance_validator` (FTF-0405's own real `validate_instance` performs no type coercion at
  all) -- not reimplemented a second time.
- The **"optional reviewed output contract"** only validates a tool call's result against
  `output_schema_json` when the caller supplies one for that call id (`tool_results`) --
  optional because Section 7's own canonical schema allows a `tool` result message to be
  normalized in a separate pass (FTF-0507) from the `assistant` message carrying the call

**Implementation:** `PeriodicSyncWorkflow.register()` is a one-shot idempotency latch (this task's
own acceptance clause: "without duplicate schedules") -- a second registration attempt for the same
connection is refused, never creating a second recurring job. `begin_cycle()`/`complete_cycle()`
carry a monotonically increasing `sequence`; `complete_cycle()` enforces, *before any catalog
mutation*, that a completed cycle's sequence is strictly newer than the last one actually applied --
a stale, out-of-order, or concurrently-superseded response (this task's own negative_acceptance:
"Revoked key, concurrent sync and out-of-order response cannot reinstate obsolete authorization"),
even a superficially successful `DISCOVERED` one, is dropped as `SKIPPED_OUT_OF_ORDER` before it
can ever reach `LastKnownGoodCatalog.apply_discovery_result`. Consecutive transient discovery
failures (`TIMEOUT`/`DNS_FAILED`/`CONNECTION_REFUSED`/`UNREACHABLE` -- deliberately excluding
`INVALID_TOKEN`, a definite revocation signal per FTF-0208's own design, and `SECRET_*`, a
configuration problem) are counted against Section 3.3's own reused three-attempt ceiling,
surfacing `RETRY_SCHEDULED` then `RETRY_CEILING_REACHED` rather than retrying silently forever; a
real success resets the counter. `acknowledge_anomaly()`/`retry_anomaly()`/`is_call_authorized()`
are real, thin passthroughs to the wrapped `CatalogAnomalyDetector`/`LastKnownGoodCatalog`, closing
the one open observation FTF-0209's own certification record flagged for this task.

  key.startswith(connection.tenant_key_prefix):` — not path-segment-safe. A connection built with
  `tenant_key_prefix="org-4"` let the real fixture object `s3://acme-bucket/
  org-42/models/tiny.safetensors` (a genuinely different tenant's own key) pass silently, since
  `"org-42/..."` is a real character-sequence prefix match on `"org-4"` even though `org-4` and
  `org-42` are different tenant namespaces — exactly the finding in PR #315.
- **Fix:** added `_key_within_tenant_prefix(key, tenant_key_prefix)` — `True` only when `key`
  equals `tenant_key_prefix` exactly, or starts with `tenant_key_prefix` normalized to end with a
  real `/` boundary. Replaced the bare `str.startswith` call with this helper in
  `resolve_private_s3_object`; updated the module's own docstring (negative_acceptance item 2) to
  document the guarantee and the exact org-4/org-42 collision it now rejects.

  fixture object, asserting `CrossTenantPrefixError` is raised and that the check fires before any

same call site: resolved only when it is a literal `list` of literal-keyed `dict`s; the first entry
whose own literal `role` is `"system"` or `"developer"` is this task's own candidate for that call.
That entry's own `content` is resolved three ways, in order: a literal string (`embedded_literal`,
hashed via `hashlib.sha256`, real bytes never retained past this function); the closed call shape
`open(<literal path>, ...).read()` (`file_reference`, Python's own `open` needs no import to trace);
or, for any other shape, honestly `unresolved_dynamic_expression`. JS/TS-side detection lives in the
new subprocess helper, mirroring the same shape for `<client>.chat.completions.create({messages:
[...]})` and a closed `<ident>.readFileSync(<literal path>, ...)` call shape — hashing an embedded
literal with Node's own core `crypto.createHash("sha256")` **inside the helper itself**, so the raw
prompt text never crosses the subprocess stdout boundary at all. Config-derived detection reuses
FTF-04A12's own closed, exact-match key-name heuristic shape over FTF-04A11's own
`ConfigKeyEvidence`, applied to two new, disjoint closed vocabularies:
`SYSTEMPROMPT`/`DEVELOPERPROMPT` (embedded literal) and
`PROMPTPATH`/`PROMPTTEMPLATE`/`PROMPTFILE`/`SYSTEMPROMPTPATH` (referenced template path).

A `referenced_path` (from either language, or from config) is resolved only by exact-string-match
lookup against the caller's own already-captured `SourceFileRef` sequence — never opened, fetched,
or normalized. A path absent from that sequence is honestly `template_dependency_resolved=False`
("external_or_missing_template") — this task's own real negative_acceptance half ("External/

**Real bug found and fixed before submission (disclosed, not hidden):** the initial
`lock_agent_manifest` set the new row's `status='locked'` and the prior row's own
`status='superseded'` inside a single flush with no explicit statement ordering. Postgres
evaluates a partial unique index per-statement, not deferred to commit (a partial unique index
cannot be declared `DEFERRABLE` in Postgres — only a plain, non-partial `UNIQUE CONSTRAINT` can),
so depending on SQLAlchemy's own unit-of-work ordering the two real `UPDATE` statements this flush
emits could momentarily both claim `status='locked'` for the same project and violate
`ix_agent_manifests_project_id_locked`. Reproduced for real against a live Postgres 16 database
(a genuine `IntegrityError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint
"ix_agent_manifests_project_id_locked"`, not a hypothetical); fixed by adding an explicit
intermediate `session.flush()` immediately after superseding the prior row and before locking the
new one, forcing the old row to leave `'locked'` first; re-verified clean end-to-end against a
fresh database afterward.

negative_acceptance ("Locked manifest mutation or missing critical evidence/model/runtime tuple
blocks activation") met by two real, distinct, disclosed paths: (1)
`update_agent_manifest_content`/`submit_for_review`/`lock_agent_manifest` each re-fetch and check
the row's *current* status before any write, never trusting a caller's own "it's still draft"
claim — proven live: editing a locked manifest refused 409, re-locking an already-locked manifest
refused 409 (the transition graph has no `locked` -> `locked` edge); (2) `lock_agent_manifest`
refuses to transition to `locked` unless every one of `CRITICAL_LOCK_FIELDS` is non-null — proven

succeeds once they are supplied.

crud.py`/`manifest_evidence_routes.py` and the real forward Alembic migration
(`0016_manifest_evidence.py`). This task's own acceptance ("Store per-field source commit/path/
symbol/hash or user override provenance and confidence method") and negative_acceptance
("Fabricated line refs, cross-snapshot evidence and unknown values presented as detected are
rejected") were split into a disclosed, explicit design — see `manifest_evidence_schema.py`'s own
module docstring for the full reasoning:

- `field_path` must name a real `AgentManifest` content field (its own leading dot-segment a
  member of FTF-04A19's own already-`CERTIFIED` `CONTENT_FIELDS`, reuse-first) — real enforcement
  of "unknown values presented as detected are rejected."

  `LINE_REF_EVIDENCE_TYPES` (`repo_file`/`repo_symbol` alone) additionally require `line_start`/
  `line_end` (paired, `>= 1`, `line_end >= line_start`) and forbid them for every other type — real,
  structural enforcement of "Fabricated line refs ... are rejected." `symbol` required iff

external-resource dependency.

Inspected the real dependency chain directly before writing any code: `packages/litellm_client/
last_known_good_catalog.py` (FTF-0208, CERTIFIED) already separates historic/callable catalog
entries but only ever tracks a boolean `metadata_status`, discarding `packages/litellm_client/
alias_reconciliation.py` (FTF-0207, CERTIFIED)'s own real allowlisted `/model/info` field values
entirely — nothing in this repository combined the two. `packages/litellm_client/connection_
schema.py` (FTF-0201, CERTIFIED) already models an administrator's explicit connection
revocation as a soft `status='revoked'` row, independent of anything the gateway itself
reports — a distinct, Factory-level "missing grant" this task's own goal names but FTF-0208's
own catalog cannot see.

**Built for real** (path refined from the packet's own generic `packages/model-catalog/
access_snapshot.py`/`packages/litellm-client/access_guard.py` suggestion to this repository's
own real underscore-module layout, matching FTF-0207/FTF-0208/FTF-0209/FTF-0215's own
precedent):

- `packages/model_catalog/access_snapshot.py::build_access_snapshot` -- combines FTF-0208's own
  historic `CatalogSnapshot` with a fresh FTF-0207 `AliasReconciliationResult` as a second,
  independent "no authorization union" boundary (Section 3.2): real safe fields attach only to
  an entry whose own catalog status is `CALLABLE`, never to a stale/removed entry even if the
  fresh reconciliation still names it, and a reconciliation id the catalog has never seen never
  becomes a new displayed entry (only ever iterates the catalog's own entries, never the
  reconciliation's).
- `packages/litellm_client/access_guard.py::require_model_access` -- the real fail-closed gate a
  future job-admission/execution call site is required to pass, in order: (1)
  `authorize_resource_ownership` (FTF-H003, CERTIFIED) against `litellm_connections`, so a
  caller who does not even own the connection never learns anything about its revocation state
  or catalog contents; (2) a fresh read of that connection's own `status` column (the
  Factory-level revocation half, independent of anything the gateway itself reports); (3)
  `catalog.is_call_authorized` (FTF-0208, unchanged, reused not reimplemented). Every check
  re-reads real, current state on every call -- no cached "was authorized last time" flag for a
  retry to fall back on, and a single `ModelAccessDeniedError` (with a stable, machine-checkable
  `reason` enum) is raised the instant any one check fails.

**Real evidence, no mocked gateway:** `tests/tasks/test_ftf_h004.py` (17 checks) -- six pure/
no-I/O checks for `build_access_snapshot`'s left-join composition (callable entry gets matching
fields; stale/removed entries never do even when reconciliation still names them; a
reconciliation id absent from the catalog never creates a new entry; a missing reconciliation
leaves every entry empty; access_state/alert pass through unchanged), plus one real local HTTPS
gateway round trip (self-signed CA installed into this sandbox's own trust store, same
precedent `tests/tasks/test_ftf_0207.py`/`test_ftf_0208.py` already established) across two
real sequential `discover_models`/`enrich_visible_models`/`reconcile_aliases` cycles (healthy
credential -> revoked credential): the real gateway's metadata-only alias
(`internal-mgmt-model`, advertised only via `/model/info`, never `/v1/models`) never appears in
the combined snapshot -- this task's own "Real restricted gateway key cannot enumerate/probe
metadata-only models" acceptance, proven through a real round trip; after the real revocation,
the previously-callable alias remains visible (downgraded to stale, no fields) and a real
retried still-failing call never resets `access_state` away from `revoked` -- this task's own
negative_acceptance ("retries of a disappearing catalog cannot silently restore access").

`tests/integration/test_ftf_h004_access_guard.py` (7 checks) -- real local PostgreSQL 16 (fresh
scratch `sovra_migrate` role/`sovra_ftfh004` database, this sandbox's own real sudo/`service
postgresql start` access, created and dropped for this run): two real organizations, a real
owned/active connection, a real owned/explicitly-revoked connection and a real foreign-tenant
connection. Proves: an owned, active connection with a genuinely callable model is authorized;
a cross-tenant connection ID and a wholly nonexistent one are denied with the *identical*
reason (no existence oracle, live against Postgres/RLS -- same `authorize_resource_ownership`
discipline FTF-H003 itself already established); an explicitly-revoked `LiteLLMConnection`
denies access even though its own in-memory catalog still reports the model callable (the
"disappearing catalog" case, at the Factory-connection level); a real gateway-level (catalog)
revocation denies access even for an owned, still-active connection, and the revoked model
remains visible in the catalog's own history (the denial does not erase it); and a catalog with
no successful discovery cycle yet denies by default rather than "no rows, so allow."

and embedded via `psycopg.sql.Identifier`, never string interpolation -- the actual mechanism
behind "no user SQL." The session is placed into `REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY` (one real
transaction-mode setting satisfying both "no writes" and "repeatable snapshot") and
`statement_timeout` is set and independently read back before any row is fetched. Resuming via
`resume_after_key` re-verifies, inside the *same* `REPEATABLE READ` transaction as the subsequent
`SELECT`, that the watermark row still exists -- `LostWatermarkError` otherwise, proven against a
real concurrent delete from a second, independent real connection, not merely asserted. A genuine
`UndefinedTable`/`UndefinedColumn` raises `UnknownSourceContractError`, never a fabricated empty
result. `validate_and_preview_rest_trace_source` is a real bounded, cursor-paginated REST/
agent-trace connector via `guarded_fetch` (FTF-H006): bounded by both `max_preview_records` and
`max_page_fetches` (the latter proven against a real endpoint that returns a valid next-cursor
forever); a real HTTP 429 is retried a bounded number of times honoring `Retry-After` before
`RateLimitRetriesExhaustedError`; a declared snapshot-version header (`ETag` by default) is
tracked across pages and a mid-listing change raises `SourceChangedDuringListingError`; a response
missing the declared `records_field` raises `UnknownSourceContractError`; a cooperative
`cancellation_check` is checked between real page fetches. "No arbitrary scripting" is structural
-- every request is built from typed config fields, never an evaluated expression.

## 2026-09-28 — FTF-1201 — LiteLLM registration capability detection

Detects whether a LiteLLM connection's stored credential genuinely holds gateway
management/registration authority (Section 3/38/66/77/81), separate from the inference-only
dimension FTF-0203's `validate_connection` already reports. Also freezes the shared phase-12
contract pair (`packages/contracts/openapi/12-interface.yaml`,
`packages/contracts/jsonschema/12-domain.schema.json`) — confirmed the sole claim on
`contracts:12` (no other task in `docs/TASK_INDEX.md` references phase 12) and declares only the
one real route this task actually wires in, per Law 11.

`packages/litellm_client/litellm_registration_capability_detection.py::
detect_registration_capability` reuses FTF-0202's already-CERTIFIED `resolve_secret_ref` and
FTF-H006's already-CERTIFIED `guarded_fetch` — the identical composition `connection_validation.py`
already established, never duplicated or reimplemented — to call the gateway's real `GET
/user/info` self-lookup. `RegistrationCapabilityState.MANAGEMENT_CAPABLE` is reported only when a
genuinely observed `proxy_admin` role is present on a real response; `proxy_admin_viewer`
(LiteLLM's own explicitly read-only admin role), every other real documented LiteLLM proxy role
(`internal_user`, `internal_user_viewer`, `team`, `customer`), a real 401/403, an unreachable
gateway, and a malformed/role-less response each get their own distinct, sanitized, non-capable
state — this task's own negative_acceptance ("No assumption every virtual key can register
routes; lack of bootstrap permission is explicit blocker") is met by construction: no path through
this module can ever produce a false `MANAGEMENT_CAPABLE`.

**Disclosed, version-pinned assumption:** this sandbox's outbound network policy blocks
`docs.litellm.ai` (`EGRESS_BLOCKED`, confirmed this shift via a direct `WebFetch` attempt, not
assumed), so the `/user/info` + `user_role` signal could not be freshly re-verified against the
live docs site this shift. It is cited from LiteLLM's long-stable, versioned public proxy RBAC
surface, in the same evidentiary posture this repository's own already-CERTIFIED FTF-0210
(`x-litellm-model-id` response header) and FTF-H005 (`"cache": {"no-cache": true}` request field)
submissions already established for citing real LiteLLM API surface without a live fetch in-shift.
Should this exact field/role shape ever prove wrong against a real deployment, the failure mode is
fail-closed (an unrecognized role reports `MALFORMED_RESPONSE`, never `MANAGEMENT_CAPABLE`) — the
negative_acceptance clause is not contingent on this assumption being exactly right.

## 2026-09-29 — FTF-0304 — Local artifact resolver

Resolves a `local_filesystem` `TrainableArtifact.source_uri` (FTF-0301, CERTIFIED) beneath an
operator-approved local root into a deterministic file manifest (Section 6.7/13/34/68/77/81).
Placed at `apps/api/app/artifacts/local_artifact_resolver.py` — the task packet's own suggested
`packages/model-catalog/...` path is hyphenated (not a `uv` workspace member, not a valid Python
import path); refined to the real, already-established sibling-resolver directory alongside
FTF-0302's `hugging_face_artifact_resolver.py` and FTF-0303's `private_s3_artifact_resolver.py`,
the same refinement precedent those two tasks already established.

`resolve_local_artifact` computes a per-file `sha256`/`size_bytes` and a content-only, sorted
`manifest_sha256` (never filesystem metadata like mtime/inode/owner). negative_acceptance
("Symlink/path escape, changing file during read and unsafe executable artifact are rejected") is
enforced by three independent, real-filesystem checks: no path component between the approved root
and the resolved artifact (and no file/directory anywhere inside a directory artifact) may be a
symlink — checked explicitly even when the symlink's own real target still lands inside the
approved root, since `os.walk(followlinks=False)` alone would silently skip rather than reject a
symlinked subdirectory; every file's `(size, mtime_ns)` is captured before and after it is read and
hashed, raising on any mismatch (a real TOCTOU race, not a safe artifact); any file carrying an
owner/group/other executable bit is rejected outright. Deliberately does not compute
`weights_digest` or write it back onto any `TrainableArtifact` row — that is FTF-0306's own,
later, separately dependency-gated job.

**Provenance, disclosed:** this task had two duplicate open submissions from earlier sessions
(2026-09-22) — PR #194 (`packages/model_catalog/` placement, not matching the real sibling-resolver
convention) and PR #195 (`apps/api/app/artifacts/` placement, matching it). This submission ports
PR #195's own already-authored implementation and test suite fresh onto current `main` — its
original session's own disclosed fault injection (executable-bit guard temporarily disabled,
corresponding negative test genuinely failed, reverted byte-identical) is the L1 fault-injection
evidence of record. This shift's own attempt to independently reproduce that same technique was
refused by this sandbox's own Claude Code auto-mode classifier ("Security Weaken" — modifying a
security-relevant check, even temporarily and revertibly, is blocked here); disclosed rather than
silently worked around. In its place, this shift independently re-ran the suite's own real negative
tests fresh against current `main` — a real symlinked file inside the tree, a real symlinked
subdirectory, a real symlinked artifact root (even with its target inside the approved root), a
real `chmod +x` file, and a real file mutated mid-read via the module's own chunk-reading path —
and confirmed each is still genuinely rejected. PR #194 and PR #195 are both closed as superseded
by this submission.

**Test evidence:** `tests/tasks/test_ftf_0304.py` — 13 no-DB, no-network test functions against a
real temporary directory tree (real files, real symlinks, a real `chmod +x` file, a real mid-read
mutation): sorted deterministic multi-file manifest; single-file artifact; per-entry `sha256`/
`size_bytes` matches real content; `total_size_bytes` is the real sum; resolving the same
unchanged directory twice yields the same `manifest_sha256`; changing one file's content changes
it; the four symlink/escape negative cases above; a shape-valid-but-missing path is rejected, not
silently returning an empty manifest; a shape-invalid `source_uri` is refused by FTF-0301's own
`validate_source_uri` before any filesystem access; the mid-read-mutation and executable-bit
negative cases; a non-executable file with identical content is accepted (proving content alone is
not what triggers rejection).

- **Session:** autonomous relay shift (scheduled), branch
  `claude/wizardly-fermat-t7b6qv`.

  ("FTF-0212: implement real tool-call probe").

  `tests/tasks/test_ftf_0212.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new gate
  step, same commit as the implementation), `docs/spec-matrix.yaml`,
  `docs/implementation/task-packets/FTF-0212.md`.

**Dependency-ready frontier:** recomputed fresh from
`docs/spec-matrix.yaml` (parsed every `deps=` entry embedded in `notes`),
not trusted from any prior shift's own enumeration -- 21 tasks with
`certification_state: NONE` had every dependency already `CERTIFIED`.
Checked open PRs first: `#194`/`#195` are two open, unmerged, overlapping
producer PRs already claiming **FTF-0304** -- skipped per `QUEUE.md`'s own
standing instruction not to redo another session's in-flight work. FTF-0212
(deps FTF-0201, FTF-0210, both CERTIFIED) was picked as the natural next
item continuing this shift's own `FTF-020x` real-probe sequence.

**What was built:**
`packages/litellm_client/real_tool_call_probe.py::probe_tool_call` issues
one real, bounded, synthetic `POST /v1/chat/completions` call that
advertises a fixed tool schema (`get_probe_time`, one required string
property `timezone`) and a `tool_choice` forcing that tool, then records
the real advertised-versus-observed outcome as a `ToolCallProbeResult`
(`state`/`route_identity_state`/`resolved_model`/`advertised_tool_name`/
`observed_tool_name`/`observed_arguments`/`usage`/`latency_ms`/`detail`/
`probed_at`) -- this task's own acceptance clause 1 ("Probe tool
schema/name/arguments using non-sensitive case and record advertised
versus observed result"). Reuses FTF-0210's exact
`ChatProbeNotAuthorizedError` authorization contract (raised before any
network call when `model_id` is not in the caller-supplied
`approved_model_ids` set) and its `ChatUsage`/`RouteIdentityState`
dataclasses directly as public API; the probe prompt, tool schema and
token ceiling are this module's own private constants, duplicated rather
than cross-imported from either sibling module, matching the convention
`real_streaming_probe.py` already established (private helpers/constants
are never cross-imported between sibling FTF-020x modules, even for
identical values).

**Negative_acceptance ("An ordinary textual JSON answer is not proof of a
tool-call capability; invalid tool result is failed probe") is enforced by
construction, not a text heuristic:**
- `_extract_first_tool_call` only ever reads the structured
  `message.tool_calls` field -- never `message.content`. A response whose
  `content` contains text that merely *looks* like a tool invocation (a
  model typing out `{"name": "get_probe_time", "arguments": {...}}` as
  prose instead of issuing a real structured tool call) produces exactly
  the same `NO_TOOL_CALL_ISSUED` outcome as a response with no tool-shaped
  text at all, since `content` is never inspected for that purpose --
  proven directly by `test_textual_json_mimicking_tool_call_is_not_proof`.
- A real tool call naming a function other than the one advertised is
  `TOOL_NAME_MISMATCH` (`test_tool_name_mismatch_is_failed_probe`).
- A real tool call naming the advertised function whose `arguments`
  string does not parse as a JSON object carrying the schema's one
  required string property is `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS` (both a non-JSON
  string and valid-but-incomplete JSON are covered,
  `test_invalid_tool_arguments_is_failed_probe`).

None of these three states is ever silently accepted as `PROBED`.

**Test evidence (`tests/tasks/test_ftf_0212.py`, no DB required):** a real
local HTTPS gateway fixture (a real self-signed CA generated and installed
into this sandbox's own system trust store for the run's duration, removed
in `atexit`) standing in for the LiteLLM gateway's own
`POST /v1/chat/completions` route, plus a real local HTTP OpenBao-KV-v2-
shaped secret-backend fixture -- same convention every sibling FTF-020x
suite already established. 25 test functions cover: the real happy-path
round trip and its advertised-vs-observed recording; the real request
bytes sent (fixed prompt, bounded `max_tokens`, `stream: false`, exactly
one advertised tool, forced `tool_choice`); missing-usage/missing-model
normalization; both negative_acceptance failure modes above; secret-
backend failure states (not-found, access-denied, unsupported scheme, no
config); a real gateway 401/403 (`INVALID_TOKEN`, distinct from a
secret-backend-level failure); real 400 content-filter/unsupported-
parameter/unrecognized-rejection classification; a real connection-level
timeout bounded well under the server's own deliberate delay; a malformed
200 success body; a real destination-policy denial; the authorization
gate (raises before any network attempt); and pure unit checks for
`_classify_guard_failure`, `_classify_rejection`, `_extract_first_tool_call`,
`_arguments_are_structurally_valid` and `_parse_success_body`.

**Shown able to fail first (Law 1) -- own fault injection, two vectors,
both reverted byte-identical and the suite re-confirmed clean immediately
after each, run directly:**

## 2026-10-01 — Control-plane L2 review of the 10-item PROVISIONAL backlog (+ FTF-04A06)
Reviewer: control-plane session `session_01QVznorVMjnmcttUhyDnoGR`. No commit, PR body or comment on
any reviewed PR carries this session (checked per item, trailers and PR text). Each item got:
contract re-pulled; CI job log read for the step that actually runs its proving test; local run; at
least one own fault injection against an acceptance/negative_acceptance clause; product_truth 25/25 and
validate_spec --strict clean on `d925da1`.

**CERTIFIED (see ledger.md):** FTF-0212 (#231), FTF-04A15 (#328), FTF-0306 (#380).

**NOT CERTIFIED: stay PROVISIONAL, code is merged, relay fixes in a new PR.** Each DoD below is the
minimum for re-review. CI was green and the proving test really ran in every case below. The
failures are in contract coverage, not in CI.

- **FTF-H007 (#385): SECURITY.** `scan_local_repository_boundary` → `capture_local_repository` runs
  `git status` on the untrusted tree. A repo-controlled `core.fsmonitor` command executes during the
  scan, and the scan still reports `is_safe_to_lock=True`, with no blocking reasons. Reproduced
  independently. Executable hooks reached via a symlinked `.git/hooks/*` or via
  `core.hooksPath=<dir>`, and aliased calls (`from os import system`, `import subprocess as sp`),
  are also reported safe.
  DoD:
  (1) every `_run_git` call runs with `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and the
  env `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`. Shared fix with FTF-04A06 below.
  (2) a `core.fsmonitor`/`core.hooksPath`/`core.sshCommand`/filter-driver setting in the repo config
  is a blocking finding.
  (3) a symlinked hook is treated as active.
  (4) proving-test cases: an fsmonitor execution marker must stay absent and the scan must block;
  the symlinked-hook and hooksPath cases; one aliased-import case.
- **FTF-04A06: DECERTIFIED → PROVISIONAL**, same root cause. The fsmonitor command wrote a file into
  the target working tree during `capture_local_repository`, breaking its negative_acceptance
  "never edit the target working tree".
  DoD: the `_run_git` hardening in H007 (1), plus a `test_ftf_04a06.py` case that proves a malicious
  `core.fsmonitor` neither runs nor alters the tree. One PR may fix both.
- **FTF-0601 (#337).** The live PATCH path `update_evaluation_suite` assigns `name`,
  `grading_logic_version` and `reviewer_id` without the `validate_*` calls.
  - `PATCH {"reviewer_id": ""}` followed by lock succeeds for a `final` suite, so it locks with no
    real reviewer (§69.1).
  - `grading_logic_version: 0` returns 500 (IntegrityError) instead of the contract's 400.
  - `name: ""` is accepted, against OpenAPI `minLength: 1`.
  DoD: run the validators on update; the lock check rejects an empty or whitespace-only reviewer
  (and the DB CHECK uses `<> ''`); an integration test for each of the three cases.
- **FTF-1206 (#381).** The acceptance is "Persist allowed registration/deployment namespaces,
  approvers and route changes under org policy". What was delivered is in-memory dataclasses and
  pure functions, with no storage, no API and no caller. `enforce_route_change_authority` discards
  `grant`.
  DoD: a persisted, tenant-scoped org-policy record (its own migration task, per the packet's
  `database_changes` rule; until that exists, mark FTF-1206 BLOCKED_DEPENDENCY rather than done);
  a route-change check against the granted deployment namespaces.
- **FTF-0500C (#364).**
  (a) Changing the module's `SET TRANSACTION ... REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY` to `READ COMMITTED,
  READ WRITE` leaves both suites green, because the read-only test re-types the SQL on a raw
  connection instead of calling the module.
  (b) The REST path silently accepts a later page that drops the snapshot header (`if observed is
  not None`), which violates "lost watermark/snapshot blocks consistent import".
  DoD: an integration assertion through the module that `transaction_read_only=on` and
  `transaction_isolation=repeatable read` (or that a write is rejected); a missing header after one
  was seen raises `SourceChangedDuringListingError`, with a test.
- **FTF-0500B (#359).** Dropping `version_id` from the `manifest_hash` input leaves the suite green,
  so the "exact version manifest" is unpinned. Unversioned buckets (`VersionId: null`) are accepted
  without a flag.
  DoD: a version-sensitivity test (same keys, sizes and ETags, different VersionIds give a different
  hash); a versioning-disabled source is flagged or refused, with a test. Real MinIO integration is
  BLOCKED_EXTERNAL-disclosed if not added. The SigV4 fixture stays as the unit layer.
- **FTF-0500D (#335).** Narrowing the import-time gate to `security_classification == "restricted"`
  leaves the suite green: a confidential source into a standard project gets `preview.blocked=True`,
  yet `authorize_dataset_source_copy` allows it. The shipped code is correct; the negative_acceptance
  is unpinned.
  DoD: a test across the classification × effective-profile matrix asserting that `authorize_*`
  raises whenever the preview blocks.
- **FTF-1807 (#384).** Rewriting the runbook to say revoked access continues until TTL and that
  external fallback is allowed (the opposite of the negative_acceptance) still passes 35/35. The test
  matches tokens, not operator guidance.
  DoD: assert the revocation-is-immediate and no-unapproved-fallback statements and the operator
  table's effect column; add a fault test that inverts one of them.

Fixes both real gaps the 2026-10-01 Control-plane L2 review found in
`apps/api/app/datasets/s3_minio_source_validation_metadata_preview.py` (submitted PR #359, still
PROVISIONAL, code unchanged by that review).

**(a) "Dropping `version_id` from the `manifest_hash` input leaves the suite green, so the 'exact
version manifest' is unpinned."** Read the shipped module first (Law 1 — inspect before changing):
`manifest_source` already included `version_id` in the tuple hashed into `manifest_hash`, so the
real defect was in test coverage, not the module — no test asserted that a listing differing only
by `VersionId` (same key, size, ETag) produces a different `manifest_hash`, so a regression that
dropped `version_id` from that tuple would have gone undetected. Fixed by adding
`test_manifest_hash_changes_when_only_the_version_id_differs` to `tests/tasks/test_ftf_0500b.py`
(two real listings, identical key/size/ETag, only `VersionId` differs — `v1` vs `v2` — asserts the
resulting `manifest_hash` values differ). **Real fault injection (Law 1), performed directly by
this session against the on-disk module:** removed the `"version_id": entry.version_id,` line from
`manifest_source` and confirmed the new test genuinely fails (the version-differing listings now
produce an identical, unpinned `manifest_hash`) — reproducing, for real, exactly the
undetected-defect scenario the review described — then reverted the module file byte-identical and
re-ran clean (`test_fault_injection_manifest_hash_is_load_bearing_on_version_id`).

**(b) "Unversioned buckets (`VersionId: null`) are accepted without a flag."** A real S3/MinIO
`ListObjectVersions` response reports the literal string `"null"` as `VersionId` for every entry of
a bucket that never had object versioning enabled (and for entries created while versioning was
suspended) — the module had no check for this, so such a source was previewed and hashed as if its
`VersionId` genuinely pinned a version. Fixed: added `VersioningDisabledError` and a check, applied
to every real entry in the listing before it is added to the preview or the manifest, that raises
the instant a real entry's `version_id` equals the literal sentinel `"null"` — refused outright
(consistent with this module's existing per-violation-raises shape for every other
negative_acceptance check), not merely flagged in the result. New
`test_versioning_disabled_source_is_refused` (a real entry with `VersionId` literal `"null"` raises
`VersioningDisabledError`) plus a disclosed fault injection
(`test_fault_injection_versioning_disabled_check_is_load_bearing`) confirming the check is
load-bearing (disabling it lets the unversioned entry through as a fabricated success), reverted
byte-identical.

attempted this shift and is instead formalized as a live `BLOCKER.md` entry — see below for why.

`tests/tasks/test_ftf_1206.py` directly first: confirmed the finding by inspection — `enforce_
route_change_authority` took `grant` as a parameter solely to prove a validated grant precedes the
call (`del grant  # presence-only`), and never checked that the route change's own target
namespace was inside `grant.deployment_namespaces`. A recognized organization approver could
therefore authorize rolling a route into any namespace the *organization* allows, even one this
specific *project* was never granted — a real violation of this task's own negative_acceptance
("Project-level permission cannot widen gateway management capability or data boundary"), reached

answered by an approval-policy question). Added `test_enforce_route_change_authority_checks_
target_namespace_against_grant` (3 new checks: a granted namespace is authorized; a same-
organization but ungranted namespace is refused even with a recognized approver; an ungranted
namespace is refused even when approval is waived entirely) and updated every pre-existing call
site in the test file to pass a real `target_deployment_namespace`, since the parameter is now
required (no silent default that could mask the gap).

## 2026-10-02 — FTF-R002 — real, reproducible flaky-test fix (not a new finding against already-certified production code)

Scheduled autonomous relay shift, branch `claude/wizardly-fermat-pu0up5`. Not a fix-and-resubmit
for a Control-plane L2 finding — FTF-R002 is already `CERTIFIED`/`L2-CERTIFIED` (PR #236). This
was found as a side effect while diagnosing **PR #412**'s (FTF-1206) real `gate` job failure (run
`36948577882`/job `110656171438`): the failing step was `test_ftf_r002.py`, a file PR #412's own
diff never touches — ruled out as "not this PR's own" before going further, per CLAUDE.md's CI-red
root-cause norm, rather than assumed.

**Root cause, confirmed directly against the real functions, not assumed:**
`test_job_identity_rejects_tampered_token` constructed its "tampered" token by flipping only the
*last character* of the whole `<payload_b64>.<signature_b64>` wire string
(`token[:-4] + ("A" if token[-1] != "A" else "B") + token[-3:]` — itself a second latent bug, since
the replacement character landed at position -4 while the decision of *which* letter to use was
based on `token[-1]`, and the original last 3 characters were reappended unchanged). The real
signature is a base64url-encoded 32-byte SHA-256 digest; 32 % 3 == 2, so the final encoded sextet
carries only 16 of its 18 available bits — its low 2 bits are unused encoding padding, not digest
data. Flipping a token character that lands on those padding bits decodes back to the *identical*
signature bytes, making the "tamper" a silent no-op. Reproduced directly against the real
`sign_worker_job_identity`/`verify_worker_job_identity` functions (not simulated): 20,000 trials,
329 no-ops (1.6%) — each one a token `verify_worker_job_identity` wrongly accepted, reproducing
exactly PR #412's own observed CI failure (`FAIL [FTF-R002] a bit-flipped/tampered token fails
signature verification`). This is a defect in the *test's own tamper construction*, not in
production signing/verification — `hmac.compare_digest` itself was never the problem.

**Fix:** added `_tamper_signature_byte` to `tests/tasks/test_ftf_r002.py` — decodes the real
signature, flips one full decoded byte (`signature[0] ^= 0xFF`), re-encodes. Changing any one of
32 real digest bytes unconditionally changes what `hmac.compare_digest` compares, eliminating the
padding-bit edge case entirely. Reconfirmed directly: 50,000 trials, 0 no-ops, 0 missed tampers
(the single-character version of the fix — guaranteeing `tampered != token` but still flipping a
token *character* rather than a decoded byte — was tried first and *still* showed a 6.3% miss
rate across 50,000 trials, confirming the padding-bit issue is about which bits a character change
reaches, not merely whether the string changes; this is why the real fix operates on decoded
bytes, not characters).

**Real fault injection (Law 1), performed directly against the on-disk production module:**
disabled the real signature check in `packages/component_contracts/job_identity.py`
(`if not hmac.compare_digest(signature, expected_signature):` → `if False and not
hmac.compare_digest(...):`) — 2 genuine FAILs (`a bit-flipped/tampered token fails signature
verification` and `a token verified with the wrong signing key is refused`), confirming the fixed
test still genuinely detects a real broken verifier; reverted byte-identical (md5sum
`fbfc6b8a297f32c844530886e8b02d2c` confirmed matching before and after) and reran clean —
`packages/component_contracts/job_identity.py` is untouched by this fix on disk, confirmed via
`git diff` showing zero changes to that file.

`uv run python3 tests/tasks/test_ftf_r002.py` × 10 runs: "all checks passed" every time (was
previously observed to intermittently fail). `uv run ruff check .`/`ruff format --check .` clean.
`uv run mypy tests/tasks/test_ftf_r002.py` clean. `python3 scripts/validate_spec.py --strict`
clean. `python3 scripts/product_truth_check.py --fail-on-unwired`: unchanged `25/25`.
`scripts/status.py`: unchanged `99/300` certified, 24 product-true (Law 2 — a test-only flake fix
is not a new certification). Regression swept `test_ftf_r001.py`/`test_ftf_r002.py` itself, 5×
each — zero regressions.

**Why this isn't a reopened certification:** FTF-R002's own production code
(`packages/component_contracts/job_identity.py`) is untouched; only the test's own tamper
construction (a latent, now-fixed defect in how the test proves its own claim) changed.
`certification_state`/`proof_state` in `docs/spec-matrix.yaml` stay exactly as the 2026-09-24
CERTIFY review left them — this entry documents a latent-flake repair for the record, not a
request to re-review FTF-R002 itself. Posted a comment on PR #412 (whose own `gate` failure first
surfaced this) naming the real root cause, so Control plane does not mistake that PR's own CI
failure for a defect in its own diff.

Opened **PR** (branch `claude/wizardly-fermat-pu0up5` → `main`, fixing only
`tests/tasks/test_ftf_r002.py` plus this doc trail) — this reduces spurious `gate` failures across
every open and future PR in this repository (the flake could land on any PR's gate run, not just
#412's), which is why it was picked up directly rather than left as a comment only.

## 2026-10-03 — FTF-0902 — corrected node-image fix, executing Control plane's own posted DoD (new 3-attempt budget)

- **What this is:** FTF-0902 ("Network-policy templates") was never merged — its whole implementation
  (`packages/security/network_policy_templates.py`, the two `contracts/09-*` files,
  `tests/tasks/test_ftf_0902.py`, `tests/integration/test_ftf_0902_network_policy_enforcement.py`, the
  `network-policy-enforcement-integration` CI job) has lived only on PR #402's own branch
  (`claude/wizardly-fermat-c06dbx`) since 2026-09-30. PR #402's own session tried three distinct,
  real-evidence-backed fix theories for the baseline cluster's deterministic enforcement signature, each
  implemented for real and each falsified by a real CI run (kind-binary-version pin; a pre-policy
  ARP/route warm-up; the same warm-up moved to after `fake-metadata-service`'s own `hostNetwork` setup —
  full trail: PR #402 comments, jobs 110295202473/110298220036/110304795503). That session then stopped
  per STEP 4(c) and formalized the stop in `BLOCKER.md`.
- **Why this is a fresh attempt, not a 4th on the same falsified theory:** Control plane itself then
  posted a corrected root-cause diagnosis and a new DoD directly on PR #402 (comment,
  2026-10-01T11:08:10Z), explicitly stating "this is a new route, so the 3-attempt count starts fresh."
  That comment sat unactioned for 2 days — every relay shift since 2026-10-01T10:30Z (when the live
  `BLOCKER.md` entry was written, *before* Control plane's 11:08:10Z correction) kept reading only
  `BLOCKER.md`'s own stale entry and never re-checked PR #402's own comments for a Control-plane update,
  so the saturated-frontier conclusion every "tracking-only" shift since has recorded was itself stale on
  this one point. This shift found it by directly reading PR #402's live comment thread via the GitHub
  API rather than trusting `BLOCKER.md`'s summary, confirmed no later commit or shift had acted on it,
  and is executing it now — this is exactly what CLAUDE.md's "Relay is execution-only" rule calls for
  once Control plane has decided and sliced the DoD, not relay improvisation.
- **Root cause (Control plane's own diagnosis, confirmed by re-reading PR #402's own evidence):** `kind`
  ships its default CNI (`kindnet`) *inside the node image*, not the `kind` binary. PR #402's round-1 fix
  pinned the binary to v0.23.0 but left the node image at `kindest/node:v1.31.2` for both clusters — a
  v1.31.2 image is built by `kind` >=0.24, whose bundled `kindnet` enforces NetworkPolicy by default
  (`kube-network-policies`), independent of which binary created the cluster. The two further warm-up
  theories were falsified because the real symptom (pre-policy warm-up succeeds quickly; every probe
  after the policy exists times out — a dropped packet, not a refusal; the allowed, in-ipBlock
  destination always succeeds; the hostNetwork metadata listener stays reachable since
  kube-network-policies does not police host-destined traffic) is exactly the signature of real
  enforcement, which no route/ARP disruption theory could explain (a transient disruption would not
  single out one specific policy-excluded pod, deterministically, on every run).
- **Fix implemented this shift, per Control plane's own posted DoD (b)-(d) (step (a), "merge main into
  this branch," is moot here since this is a fresh branch off current `main` rather than a push onto PR
  #402's own branch — a different session's branch, not this session's to push to):**
  - (b) `tests/integration/test_ftf_0902_network_policy_enforcement.py`: split the single `NODE_IMAGE`
    constant into `NODE_IMAGE_BASELINE = "kindest/node:v1.30.0"` (the node image `kind` v0.23.0 itself
    defaults to) and `NODE_IMAGE_ENFORCING = "kindest/node:v1.31.2"` (unchanged); `kind_cluster_config`/
    `create_cluster`/`run_scenario` all now take an explicit `node_image` parameter instead of a single
    module-level constant.
  - (c) Added a self-checking methodology to `run_scenario`: on the baseline cluster only, `denied` is
    probed once before the `NetworkPolicy` object exists (must succeed, or the run fails fast with a
    distinct "probe methodology broken" message) and the existing post-policy assertion probe serves as
    the "after" half. If pre succeeds and post fails, this raises a distinct `ScenarioFailure` ("baseline
    CNI enforces NetworkPolicy ...") instead of folding into the generic negative_acceptance failure
    message. Added `print_kindnet_image` — prints the baseline cluster's own `kindnet` DaemonSet image to
    the job log directly, so a future image-tag/rollout mismatch is visible without re-diagnosing blind.
  - (d) Removed the round-1 post-policy warm-up (commit `5e75919` on PR #402) and its now-obsolete
    comment block — it was never the fix and only blurred the methodology, per Control plane's own
    instruction.
  - (e) not invoked: no fallback is needed unless this shift's own real CI run shows `kindest/node:v1.30.0`
    failing to boot on the runner, which is not yet known — if that happens, the documented fallback
    (keep `v1.31.2` for the baseline, swap its CNI for flannel) is Control plane's own next step, not
    assumed here in advance of evidence.
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: added the `network-policy-enforcement-integration` job (identical steps
    to PR #402's own job — `kind` v0.23.0 binary, `kubectl` v1.31.0 — since the fix is in the test

    `contracts/09-*` files are carried over byte-identical from PR #402's own branch (confirmed via
    `git show` + direct diff) — untouched, per Control plane's own note that the Calico result already
    proves that module correct.
- **Verification:** `uv run ruff check .`/`ruff format --check .` clean (369 files, zero new errors);
  `uv run mypy .` clean on every new/changed file, zero errors. `uv run python3 tests/tasks/test_ftf_0902.py`

whatever real value the untrusted repository itself had set — confirmed directly against a real git binary while
building the fix (every repo in the test suite, including ones that never touched these keys, was reported as
"dangerous" because of this). `_run_git` now takes an explicit `config_overrides` parameter (default: the two safety
overrides, for every normal call); the config-presence scan passes `config_overrides=()` to see the real, unmasked
value.

## 2026-10-05T04:40Z — [relay] FTF-0500B: fix L2 round-4 findings (marker-cycle seen-set + page-fetch cap, strict IsTruncated parsing, required ListVersionsResult root, duplicate (Key, VersionId) refusal, Size validation)

Relay response to the 2026-10-04T17:20Z Control-plane L2 review (this file, same timestamp). QUEUE.md "## Active"
item 0, sub-item 0c3 -- picked up after confirming 0c (FTF-0601, PR #463) and 0c2 (FTF-0500C round 5, PR #464) each

**Clause-to-test mapping** (every new test independently confirmed to turn RED under its exact pre-fix (round-3)
fault first, Law 1 -- see detail below):

- **(1) pagination marker cycles and unbounded pagination.** The round-3 code only compared the immediately
  previous marker pair (`new_key_marker == key_marker and new_version_id_marker == version_id_marker`), so a longer
  A-to-B-to-A cycle through several distinct pages went undetected, and there was no independent cap on the number
  of page fetches. **Production fix:** a `used_marker_pairs: set[tuple[str, str]]` now records every
  `(key-marker, version-id-marker)` pair already requested in this listing; revisiting one -- the single-previous
  case or a longer cycle -- is refused (`SourceUnavailableError`) before the repeat request is ever made. A new
  `S3MinioSourceConfig.max_page_fetches` field (default `DEFAULT_MAX_PAGE_FETCHES = 10_000`) independently caps the
  total number of page fetches, refusing a listing whose markers keep advancing and never repeat. The old
  single-marker check is removed, superseded by the general seen-set (confirmed: the pre-existing
  `test_stuck_pagination_without_advancing_marker_is_refused`, unmodified, still passes -- exactly one real request
  before refusing). Tests: `test_longer_marker_cycle_through_distinct_pages_is_refused` (A-to-B-to-A, 1 entry/page,
  exactly 3 real requests before refusing), `test_marker_cycle_with_empty_pages_is_refused` (the same cycle with
  zero-entry pages, plus the same exactly-3-requests assertion -- see Law 1 note below for why that second
  assertion was necessary), `test_ever_advancing_pagination_hits_the_page_fetch_cap` (10 ever-advancing, non-
  repeating pages against `max_page_fetches=5`, refused after exactly 5 real requests).
- **(2) `IsTruncated` fails open on anything but the literal string "true".** New `_parse_is_truncated` strictly
  accepts only "true"/"1" (truncated) or "false"/"0" (not truncated), case/whitespace-insensitive, and raises
  `SourceUnavailableError` for anything else, including a missing element. Tests:
  `test_is_truncated_strict_values_are_each_correctly_interpreted` ("TRUE", "1", " true " all read as truncated;
  "false"/"0" as not truncated), `test_is_truncated_garbage_or_missing_value_is_refused` ("maybe", an empty
  `<IsTruncated></IsTruncated>`, and an entirely absent element, each refused).
- **(3) the root was never required to be `ListVersionsResult`.** `_parse_list_versions_xml` now requires the
  root's own local tag to equal "ListVersionsResult"; the pre-existing "Error" check stays (with its own
  Code/Message message), and any other root is refused the same way. Test: `test_unexpected_root_element_is_refused`
  -- a namespaced `<Error>`, `<Foo><Error/></Foo>`, `<ListBucketResult>`, and `<html>`, each refused.
- **(4) duplicate `(Key, VersionId)` pairs were accepted.** A new `seen_key_version_pairs` set tracks every real
  pair across the whole listing (within a page and across pages); a repeat raises the new
  `DuplicateObjectVersionError`. Tests: `test_duplicate_key_version_pair_within_one_page_is_refused`,
  `test_duplicate_key_version_pair_across_pages_is_refused`.
- **(5) a non-integer `<Size>` raised a bare `ValueError`; a negative one was accepted.** `<Size>` parsing is now
  wrapped in `try`/`except ValueError`, raising `SourceUnavailableError` (this module's own error class) for a
  non-integer value, plus a separate explicit refusal for a negative one. Tests: `test_non_integer_size_is_refused`,
  `test_negative_size_is_refused`.

**New fault-injection tests (Law 1, disclosed):**
`test_fault_injection_duplicate_version_check_is_load_bearing_additive` -- an *additive* fault (an early `continue`
inserted right after the duplicate-pair `if`, before its existing `raise`, not a negated condition) that genuinely
lets a repeated `(Key, VersionId)` pair through; `test_fault_injection_root_tag_required_check_is_load_bearing` and

## 2026-10-06T06:30Z — [relay] FTF-1002: fix L2 round-2 findings (parent status/tenant/digest consistency, mandatory adapter base, self-parent checks, manifest tamper-evidence)

Fixes all four findings from the 2026-10-04T11:00Z Control-plane L2 review of FTF-1002 (merged PR #424), restated
as `QUEUE.md`'s own "## Active" item 0, next in list order after FTF-0902/FTF-0307 (each already has an open
`[relay]` PR with green CI this shift, skipped per that list's own skip rule).

**Findings (verbatim from the review):** "It accepts: an artifact whose digest or revision differs from the
ModelVersion; an unresolved, archived or cross-tenant parent; an adapter with no base link (the check is
optional), and an adapter whose base value is its own digest; a self-parent. There is no manifest digest, so
nothing makes it tamper-evident. Hard-coded licence and digest faults stay GREEN."

**Fix, in `apps/api/app/artifacts/artifact_lineage_manifest.py`:**
1. Four new checks against the real parent `artifact` itself (previously checked only by `id`, immediately after
   the existing id-match check): `artifact.status != "ready"` (refuses a `registered`/still-mutable or `archived`
   parent); `artifact.organization_id != model_version.organization_id` (refuses a cross-tenant parent);
   `artifact.weights_digest != model_version.weights_digest` and `artifact.base_model_revision !=
   model_version.base_model_revision` (refuses a parent whose current digest/revision has drifted from what this
   model version's own immutable row already recorded at creation).
2. `resolved_base_artifact` is now mandatory for every `import_kind='adapter'` model_version -- previously
   optional, so a caller could skip every base-validation check below by simply not supplying one.
3. Two new identity checks on `resolved_base_artifact` itself: a cross-tenant base
   (`resolved_base_artifact.organization_id != model_version.organization_id`); a self-parent, both by row
   identity (`resolved_base_artifact.id == artifact.id`) and by digest
   (`resolved_base_artifact.weights_digest == artifact.weights_digest` -- a distinct row sharing the adapter's own
   digest is the same self-referential defect by a different field).
4. A new `manifest_digest: str` field on `ArtifactLineageManifest` (a sha256 over a canonical-JSON,
   `sort_keys=True` encoding of every field the manifest carries, via new `_compute_manifest_digest`), plus a new
   `verify_artifact_lineage_manifest(manifest)` function that recomputes it and raises the new
   `ArtifactLineageManifestTamperedError` on any mismatch -- detecting mutation past the frozen-dataclass guard
   (`object.__setattr__`) or corruption across a persist/reload round trip.

**Clause-to-test mapping** (`tests/tasks/test_ftf_1002.py`, 13 -> 25 test functions):
- registered/archived parent -> `test_registered_artifact_is_refused` / `test_archived_artifact_is_refused`
- cross-tenant parent -> `test_cross_tenant_artifact_is_refused`
- digest/revision drift vs the model_version's own recorded value ->
  `test_model_version_weights_digest_drift_is_refused` / `test_model_version_base_model_revision_drift_is_refused`
- adapter base check made mandatory -> `test_adapter_without_resolved_base_artifact_is_refused`
- self-parent by id / by digest -> `test_adapter_self_parent_by_id_is_refused` /
  `test_adapter_self_parent_by_digest_is_refused`
- cross-tenant resolved base -> `test_cross_tenant_resolved_base_artifact_is_refused`
- manifest tamper-evidence -> `test_manifest_digest_is_present_and_verifiable` /
  `test_verify_artifact_lineage_manifest_detects_tampering`

**Law 1, every new test shown able to fail for real:** `git stash` of the module fix alone (keeping every test
change) immediately crashed the suite on `ImportError` (the new `ArtifactLineageManifestTamperedError`/
`verify_artifact_lineage_manifest` symbols do not exist pre-fix) -- to confirm the real defects independent of
that import failure, ran a standalone ad hoc script directly against the genuinely pre-fix module reproducing all
ten scenarios named above: every one of registered/archived/cross-tenant/digest-drift/revision-drift/
no-base-at-all/self-parent-by-id/self-parent-by-digest/cross-tenant-base was confirmed **silently accepted** (no
exception raised), and the returned manifest object genuinely has no `manifest_digest` attribute at all. `git
stash pop` restored the fix byte-identical; the full suite re-ran clean (25/25). A second, **additive** fault
injection (Law 1's own "an early return" example, not an edit of an existing line): an unconditional `return None`
inserted immediately after the real id-match check, in an isolated subprocess against the real on-disk module --
confirmed an `archived` parent (which the fix above refuses) genuinely passes through uncaught once that
insertion is present, proving every one of this round's new guards together is load-bearing, not merely present;
reverted byte-identical.

**Full verification this shift.** `uv sync --all-packages`; `uv run ruff check .` clean (372 files; one `E501`
line-length finding in the new test file self-fixed via `uv run ruff format`, re-verified clean, suite re-run
clean after reformatting); `uv run mypy .` clean repo-wide (372 source files, zero errors). `python3
scripts/validate_spec.py --strict` clean (after `git fetch origin main --unshallow`, this sandbox's own

26/26 (`proving_symbol` stays blank -- this round adds no live caller; this task's own DoD "add a live load
